$meta.name: Babel per-field validation error codes
$meta.description: The `error.field.*` family carried in the additive `fieldErrors` array of 400 responses. One entry per offending input, so a client can render the message BESIDE the field instead of as a form-level banner.

envelope.field: body-relative dotted path the client maps to an input (`email`, `items.0.name`); empty for form-level issues
envelope.message: localized per the request Accept-Language — the fallback when `code` is unknown
envelope.params: constraint values for client-side rendering; see `params` below

derivedFrom.note: Mapped from ZodIssueCode by the API, but the WIRE VALUES ARE OURS — a Zod upgrade that renames an issue kind is absorbed at the mapper and never reaches a client. `invalid_type` splits on whether the value was absent (REQUIRED) or the wrong shape (INVALID_TYPE); `invalid_string` splits on the string check (email / url / everything else). Anything unmapped becomes INVALID.

drift.note: The starkest gap of the four contracts: the server localizes all 16 in four languages, and NEITHER client ships a single translation key for any of them. Both render the server `message` verbatim, so a field error is the one part of the UI that ignores the user's language preference when the server and client disagree about it. Mobile is worse than admin: bad_request_exception.dart keeps only `message` and DISCARDS `code` and `params`, so it could not localize them today even if the keys existed.
drift.admin: 0 translation keys; code + params reach the form layer (src/lib/api-error.ts FieldErrorDetail)
drift.mobile: 0 translation keys; code + params discarded at parse (lib/common/errors/bad_request_exception.dart)
